content.title: 'The Ultimatum: Queer Love' Trailer and Release Date
content.text: For better or worse, sapphic dating drama is finally headed for the Netflix reality show industrial complex. The streaming service recently unveiled the trailer and premiere date for The Ultimatum: Queer Love, teasing plenty of queer chaos on the horizon.In case you skipped the first season of The Ultimatum, here’s the gist: the show introduces a gaggle of (usually) twenty-something couples, one of whom is ready to settle down and one of whom is not. In just eight weeks, each member of all five couples will have to pair up with another cast member “to get a glimpse of two different futures,” then choose whether or not to get married to their original partner. While the first season was all straight couples, The Ultimatum: Queer Love features a cast made up entirely of queer women and nonbinary people, which feel like a natural fit for today’s dating shows which, let’s be honest, are undeniably U-Haul-y.“You said you wanted to marry me, but you fell in love with someone else in a week and a half,” one cast member spits at their partner in the first trailer. Kudos to Netflix for bravely realizing that, yes, queer people can make for great reality TV. Better yet, this season will be free from the Nick and Vanessa Lachey jumpscares that have become customary for Netflix dating shows. Instead, The Ultimatum: Queer Love will be hosted by Sweet Magnolias star JoAnna Garcia Swisher. The series launches May 24, with additional episodes rolling out over the following weeks.Although The Ultimatum: Queer Love is the first Netflix reality dating show to feature an all-LGBTQ+ cast, it’s not the first time that queer stars have been featured on one of the channel’s dating series. Love Is Blind Season 1 featured a controversial arc in which cast members Carlton Morton and Diamond Jack broke off their engagement after Carlton told Diamond he was bisexual, resulting in a major fight between the two.More recently, former Love Is Blind and Too Hot to Handle star Francesca Farago dated Twentysomethings: Austin alum Abbey Humprheys on Perfect Match, in which cast members from various Netflix series attempt to find love with each other. Farago, who is bisexual, recently told Variety that the show’s producers didn’t originally inform her that she would have the opportunity to date both men and women.“I wasn’t even sure [dating Abbey] was going to happen because it was a heterosexual show,” Farago said. “But I’m glad that it happened, and I’m glad that that relationship happened as well. I kind of just switched up the game.”And now that The Ultimatum: Queer Love is on the horizon, the possibilities for queer reality mess are truly endless.Get the best of what’s queer.
